application_fee.details: All applicants also pay a non-refundable portal charge of Rs 200 + 18% GST. Scientist applicants pay another Rs 600 + 18% GST for the Competence Evaluation Test. The fee can only be paid online. Fee concessions apply only to candidates with M.P. domicile. PwD applicants with M.P. domicile have their fee waived as per rules.

age_limit.details: Post Maximum Age Chief Scientist 62 years Senior Scientist 50 years Scientist 40 years | SC, ST and OBC candidates get up to 5 years of age relaxation. qualification.details: SC, ST and OBC candidates get up to 5 years of age relaxation. Women (Unreserved and Reserved) and Specially Abled (Divyang) candidates also get 5 years of relaxation. RVSKVV employees have no upper age limit for the Senior Scientist and Scientist posts. | An eminent scholar with a Doctoral degree in Agronomy, Soil Science, Soil Science and Agricultural Chemistry, Agricultural Chemistry, Soil Physics, Soil Fertility, Soil Chemistry, Water Science and Technology, Soil and Conservation Engineering or Soil Conservation and Water Management. You also need at least 10 publications as books and/or research or policy papers. M.Sc. (Ag./Horti.), M.Sc. or M.Tech. in one of the subjects above, or in Conservation Agriculture, Organic Farming or Natural Farming, with at least 55% marks or equivalent OGPA. Ten years of experience in Research, Teaching, Extension Education or Farm Management. At least 3 of those years must be as a Senior Scientist or Associate Professor, or in an equivalent position at AGP Rs. 9000 (6th CPC) or Pay Level 13A (7th CPC). Experience guiding doctoral-level research counts. Published work or innovations that show your contribution. | Agronomy: Ph.D. in Agronomy, and M.Sc. (Ag.) in Agronomy with at least 55% marks or equivalent OGPA. Genetics and Plant Breeding: Ph.D. in Agriculture in Genetics and Plant Breeding or Plant Breeding and Genetics, and M.Sc. (Ag.) in the same subject with at least 55%. Entomology: Ph.D. in Agriculture in Entomology, and M.Sc. (Ag) in Entomology with at least 55%. Plant Pathology: Ph.D. in Agriculture in Plant Pathology, and M.Sc. (Ag) in Plant Pathology with at least 55%. Soil and Water Conservation Engineering: Ph.D. in Agricultural Engineering, and M.Sc., M.Tech. or M.E. in Agricultural Engineering with at least 55%. Both degrees must be in one of these specialisations: Soil and Water Engineering, Soil and Water Conservation Engineering, Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, Land and Water Management Engineering, Water Resource Technology, Water Resource Engineering, Hydrology, or Water Engineering and Management. Experience for all Senior Scientist posts: at least eight years in the relevant subject as an Assistant Professor or Scientist, or in an equivalent position, at one of these levels: Rs 8000-13500 (5th CPC) GP Rs 5400/6000 or more in PB Rs 15600-39100 (6th CPC) Pay Level 10A (7th CPC) Alternatively, eight years combining that experience with high-quality post-doctoral research (Ph.D. period excluded) and at least 5 publications. | For all Scientist posts you also need a NET pass from ICAR, UGC, CSIR or another agency approved by UGC or the Government. Biochemistry and Phytochemistry applicants may instead have NET, SLET, SET or an equivalent exam. You must also have one publication in a NAAS-rated or UGC-referred journal. | You do not need NET if you meet one of these conditions: | You hold a Ph.D. done with course work under the UGC Regulation 2009, you produce the NET exemption certificate in Annexure-I, and you have two full-length papers with a NAAS rating of at least 4. You registered for your Ph.D. before 2009 (completed before or after 2009) and have two full-length papers in journals with a NAAS rating of 4 or above. | A Ph.D. without course work does not exempt you from NET in any other case. | You must be an Indian citizen, know Hindi and be registered with Aadhaar. All qualifications must be from a recognised Indian university or an accredited foreign university, and must be complete when you apply. Fixed pay in non-government organisations, private enterprises or private colleges does not count as equivalent to the pay scales above. | For the full eligibility of each discipline, including Senior Scientist (Microbiology), see the official notification.

selection_process: Scientist applicants take a Competence Evaluation Test. Uploaded documents are scored. Documents that are illegible or unclear may not be considered and get no score. You must show all original documents at the interview or at document verification. Any shortfall in qualifications leads to rejection of the application.
how_to_apply: Go to www.rvskvv.net or the MPOnline Chayan portal between 29 October 2026 and 16 November 2026.
Read all the terms, conditions and instructions for the post you want.
Fill in the online form and upload clear, readable scans of your documents.
Check the form carefully before final submission. You cannot make corrections after that.

Do not send a printout or any documents to the university. Hard-copy applications are not accepted. Keep your original certificates and experience proofs ready for the interview or document verification. NET-exempt Ph.D. holders also need the Annexure-I certificate.

content_sections.heading: About RVSKVV
content_sections.text: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV) is an agricultural university at Raja Pancham Singh Marg, Near Akashwani, Gwalior - 474002 (M.P.). The university runs these All India Coordinated Research Projects at its various centres. The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi provides 75% of the funding and the Government of Madhya Pradesh provides 25%.

content_sections.heading: Application Fee
content_sections.text: All applicants also pay a non-refundable portal charge of Rs 200 + 18% GST. Scientist applicants pay another Rs 600 + 18% GST for the Competence Evaluation Test. The fee can only be paid online. Fee concessions apply only to candidates with M.P. domicile. PwD applicants with M.P. domicile have their fee waived as per rules.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Scientist applicants take a Competence Evaluation Test. Uploaded documents are scored. Documents that are illegible or unclear may not be considered and get no score. You must show all original documents at the interview or at document verification. Any shortfall in qualifications leads to rejection of the application.

faq.question: Q1. When can I apply for the RVSKVV Scientist posts?
faq.answer: Online applications run from 29 October 2026 to 16 November 2026.

faq.question: Q2. What is the age limit for Scientist?
faq.answer: The maximum is 40 years on 28 October 2026. SC, ST, OBC, women and Divyang candidates get 5 years of relaxation.

faq.question: Q3. Is NET compulsory for the Scientist post?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold a Ph.D. done with UGC 2009 course work, produce the Annexure-I certificate and have two full-length papers with a NAAS rating of at least 4.

faq.question: Q4. How much does a Scientist applicant pay in total fees?
faq.answer: General and OBC applicants pay Rs 1500 and SC, ST and Divyang applicants pay Rs 750. On top of that, everyone pays Rs 600 + 18% GST for the Competence Evaluation Test and a Rs 200 + 18% GST portal charge.

faq.question: Q5. Can candidates from outside Madhya Pradesh apply?
faq.answer: Yes. They are considered only in the Unreserved (UR) category and pay the UR fee.

faq.question: Q6. How much experience does a Senior Scientist need?
faq.answer: At least eight years as an Assistant Professor, Scientist or in an equivalent position, for example at Pay Level 10A. Alternatively, combined experience including post-doctoral research with at least 5 publications.

faq.question: Q7. Is there a service bond?
faq.answer: Yes. You sign a 3-year bond on Rs. 1000 stamp paper. If you leave early, you repay your salary for the remaining period.

faq.question: Q8. Who funds these AICRP posts?
faq.answer: ICAR, New Delhi pays 75% and the Government of Madhya Pradesh pays 25%.

faq.question: Q9. Do I need to post a hard copy of the application?
faq.answer: No. Applications are online only, and the university does not accept hard copies.
